3a3306d06fab2152.gloss: Refusal is handled in two layers: a retrieval score threshold (bypassing the model) and a NOT_IN_DOCS signal from the model. This makes refusal deterministic and testable, compensating for the local model's tendency to hallucinate when documents don't support an answer.

questions.q: Why add a retrieval threshold instead of letting the model refuse answers on its own?
mustMention: small local models invent/hallucinate easily
two-layer approach: threshold plus NOT_IN_DOCS signal
makes refusal deterministic and testable
measured data: threshold alone refused only 2 of 8 must-refuse cases, model's NOT_IN_DOCS signal refused the other 6

questions.q: Walk through how your two refusal layers work together. Why is the threshold a separate layer and not just part of the prompt?
mustMention: retrieval score threshold (first layer, no model call)
NOT_IN_DOCS signal from the model (second layer)
threshold is a layer underneath/before the prompt
threshold alone is insufficient: only caught 2 of 8 must-refuse questions

questions.q: How did you measure that both refusal layers are actually necessary?
mustMention: tested 8 must-refuse questions
threshold caught 2, model signal caught the other 6
empirical measurement proves both layers carry load

bbe352f42984bb44.gloss: Chose token-level detection of NOT_IN_DOCS sentinel anywhere in a response to refuse uncertain answers from a RAG-based chat agent. This is more robust than exact full-reply matching because small language models often insert words around the sentinel.

mustMention: small models add words around the sentinel

mustMention: showing a possibly-wrong answer is worse than an extra refusal
prioritizes correctness over always providing an answer

questions.q: How does your token-level detection handle the sentinel appearing in different positions within the model's response?
mustMention: NOT_IN_DOCS can appear anywhere in the response

b9a86a2c1775a9c4.gloss: The faithfulness scorer now compares numbers by type and treats source-question numbers as known context, fixing false positives from coincidental matches and false negatives from correct model data repetition.

counts the question's own numbers as known
result: identifies source numbers separately from invented ones
